newsitem.title: CHINA: China says finds footprints of bigfoot in forests.
newsitem.headline: China says finds footprints of bigfoot in forests.

text.p: Researchers hunting for China's elusive, reclusive hairy "Bigfoot" may have found footprints of the legendary creature, the Xinhua news agency said on Tuesday.

Hundreds of very large footprints resembling those of a man -- but much larger -- have been seen in the forests of the mountainous Shennongjia National Park in central Hubei province, it quoted Wang Fangchen, head of the privately run Committee for Research on Strange and Rare Creatures, as saying.
"We have made preliminary conclusions that they were left by two animals walking on two legs," it said quoting Wang, who has been hunting for the fabled creature for several years.

"The biggest footprint is 37 cm (15 inches) long, very similar to that of a man but is quite larger than man's, and is different from the footprints of a bear or any other identified animals," Wang said.
The creature that made the footprints was believed to weigh about 200 kg (440 lbs), he said.

Wang had led a team of 30 scientists on a fruitless hunt through Shennongjia last summer and had vowed to resume his search for the fabled two-metre (6 1/2-ft) red-haired human-like creature, known in local folklore as China's wildman.
Wang's team found similar footprints left by another two mysterious creatures in Shennongjia last winter, Xinhua said.

Progress toward unravelling the myth of the wildman would be of great scientific significance, Wang said, but he urged caution and warned researchers not to jump to swift conclusions without hard scientific evidence.

Theories abound about the mythical creature, with some scientists speculating it may be an unknown primate, some arguing that it may be a bear or a monkey and others suggesting it could be a missing evolutionary link between ape and human.
